💡 What: Refactored `RuleBasedNaturalLanguageTranslator.cs` to use pre-compiled static regexes (`RegexOptions.Compiled`) for frequently executed parsing patterns ('last X days', 'top X', 'first X').
🎯 Why: Calling `Regex.Match` with a string pattern internally involves caching, but compiling the regex to Intermediate Language (IL) completely avoids parsing and setup overhead on every method invocation.

author: tmchow
body:
## Summary

The existing `document-review` skill uses a single-voice reviewer that tries to evaluate planning documents across all dimensions simultaneously. This produces shallow, unfocused feedback -- the reviewer context-switches between product strategy, technical feasibility, design completeness, security, scope, and consistency without going deep on any of them.

This PR replaces that with a **multi-persona pipeline** that dispatches specialized reviewer agents in parallel, each focused on a single analytical lens:

### Always-on personas (run on every document)
- **coherence-reviewer** -- hunts contradictions, terminology drift, structural issues, broken internal references, and unresolved dependency gaps
- **feasibility-reviewer** -- evaluates whether the plan survives contact with reality: architecture conflicts, shadow path tracing (happy/nil/empty/error for every data flow), dependency gaps, migration risks, implementability

### Conditional personas (activated by content signals in the document)
- **product-lens-reviewer** -- challenges problem framing with premise inversion (Munger), trajectory checking, goal-requirement alignment, and prioritization coherence
- **design-lens-reviewer** -- dimensional 0-10 rating across information architecture, interaction states, user flows, responsive/a11y, and unresolved decisions; includes AI slop detection
- **security-lens-reviewer** -- plan-level security architecture: attack surface inventory, auth/authz gaps, data exposure, trust boundaries, and a lightweight threat model
- **scope-guardian-reviewer** -- challenges unnecessary abstractions, premature frameworks, scope-goal misalignment, and priority dependency issues

### Pipeline architecture
The orchestrator skill (SKILL.md) handles the full lifecycle:
1. **Classify** the document type and select conditional personas based on content signals
2. **Dispatch** all selected agents in parallel using fully-qualified namespace references
3. **Synthesize** findings through confidence gating, fingerprint-based dedup, cross-persona promotion of corroborated below-threshold findings, and contradiction resolution
4. **Route** findings into two buckets: auto-fixes (applied inline) and everything else (presented grouped by P0-P3 severity)
5. **Offer** iterative refinement or "Review complete" terminal signal

### Reference files
- `findings-schema.json` -- JSON schema for structured findings with 2-class autofix routing (`auto`/`present`)
- `subagent-template.md` -- shared prompt template with variable slots for consistent agent dispatch
- `review-output-template.md` -- markdown output format for the synthesized review

### Key design decisions
- **No `<examples>` blocks** -- these agents are always dispatched by the orchestrator, never auto-triggered, so triggering examples waste tokens
- **Terse agent prompts** (~40-50 lines each) -- inspired by [iterative-engineering's coherence-reviewer](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-plugins/blob/main/iterative-engineering/agents/coherence-reviewer.md) pattern; every line earns its place
- **Content-based activation** centralized in the skill, not in agent descriptions -- keeps agents focused on analysis, not self-selection
- **2-class autofix routing** (`auto`/`present`) -- findings are either deterministic fixes the orchestrator applies without asking, or they require user judgment. No middle ground needed for document review.
- **Backward-compatible terminal signal** -- "Review complete" preserved for all 4 callers (ce:plan, ce:plan-beta, ce:brainstorm, ce:work)

## Test plan
- [ ] Run `bun run release:validate` to verify plugin/marketplace consistency
- [ ] Invoke `document-review` skill on a requirements document and verify conditional persona selection
- [ ] Invoke `document-review` skill on a technical plan and verify all 6 personas activate
- [ ] Verify findings output matches review-output-template format
- [ ] Verify "Review complete" terminal signal is emitted

body:
## Objective

Introduce runtime type registration systems across core engine modules (animation, audio, assets, physics, etc.) which register types information.

## Solution

Previously, type metadata required for reflection/serialization was either:

* Missing entirely, or
* Implicitly defined and scattered across modules

This made it difficult to:

* Support reflection-driven features (serialization, inspection, tooling)
* Extend systems generically (e.g. animation effectors, asset handling)
* Maintain consistency across plugins

### Changes made

- Register the following through startup systems:

  - Components (e.g. `AudioPlayer`, `PhysicsHitbox`)
  - Resources (e.g. `AudioGraph`, `Assets<T>`)
  - Enums and opaque runtime types (e.g. `AudioBuffer`)

- Each plugin registers its types into the type registry

### Why this approach

- **Separation of concerns**: Runtime logic and type metadata are now orthogonal

- **Extensibility**: New systems/components can participate in reflection without modifying core

- **Future-proofing**: Enables upcoming features e.g

  - serialization/deserialization
  - editor tooling
  - dynamic inspection
  - reflection-driven animation
  - reflection-driven scenes

- **Consistency**: All modules follow the same registration pattern

## Showcase

N/A

## Migration guide

No user-facing breaking changes

### Notes

- Type registration is **required at startup** for reflection-dependent systems
- Order of plugin registration may matter if types are consumed early
- Some types are marked opaque (e.g. `AudioBuffer`) intentionally

## 💡 Vulnerability:
A LaTeX injection vulnerability was present in the PDF report generation logic (`backend/latex_report.py`). User-provided metadata like `patient_name`, `patient_id`, and `gender` were being directly interpolated into the `.tex` template string without escaping. An attacker could provide payloads like `\input{/etc/passwd}` or `\write18` (if shell escape was enabled) to read arbitrary files, crash the compilation process, or manipulate the generated report.

Allows users to inject arbitrary LaTeX commands, leading to denial of service (crashing the pdflatex compilation) or potential information disclosure (reading arbitrary files off the server via `\input{...}`).

- Added a robust `escape_latex` function that coerces inputs to strings and performs a single-pass character replacement for all dangerous LaTeX control characters (`\`, `{`, `}`, `%`, `$`, `&`, `#`, `^`, `_`, `~`).

- Logged the vulnerability and prevention strategy to `.jules/sentinel.md`.

body:
This PR adds the missing AArch64 implementation of the architecture-owned terminal primitive `arch_halt()` and keeps it strictly mechanical: architecture-local, non-returning, and policy-free. It mirrors the existing x86_64 halt boundary without expanding architecture abstraction or platform behavior.

- **Architecture boundary: AArch64 `arch_halt()`**
  - Added `arch/aarch64/arch_halt.c` implementing `_Noreturn void arch_halt(void)`.
  - Uses a minimal AArch64 terminal sequence in an infinite loop:
    - `msr daifset, #0xf` (mask interrupts)
    - `wfi` (enter wait-for-interrupt state)
  - Keeps behavior fully architecture-owned with no scheduler, allocation, or I/O coupling.

- **Link-time contract test (AArch64)**
  - Added `tests/arch/aarch64/test_arch_halt_link.c`.
  - Verifies symbol presence and linkage only by taking the function pointer to `arch_halt`, without executing it.
  - Keeps test scope compile/link-time and architecture-local.

- **Changelog update (`v0.0.0`)**
  - Recorded addition of the minimal AArch64 halt stub.
  - Explicitly notes it mirrors the x86_64 terminal primitive.
  - Explicitly states no policy or abstraction layer was introduced.

```c
_Noreturn void arch_halt(void)
{
#if defined(__aarch64__)
    for (;;) {
        __asm__ volatile ("msr daifset, #0xf; wfi" ::: "memory");
    }
#else
    for (;;) {
    }
#endif
}
```

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/ethervox-ai/ethervoxai/security/code-scanning/50](https://github.com/ethervox-ai/ethervoxai/security/code-scanning/50)

In general, the fix is to ensure files are created with the most restrictive permissions necessary, typically read/write for the current user only. On POSIX, this is usually done by using `open()` with an explicit mode like `S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR` when creating the file, and only then wrapping the resulting file descriptor in a `FILE*` via `fdopen()` if stream operations are needed. This avoids relying on the process `umask` and prevents accidentally creating group/world-writable files.

For this specific code, the best fix without changing functionality is to replace the direct `fopen(dest_path, "wb")` call with a POSIX-specific `open()` + `fdopen()` sequence under `#ifndef _WIN32`, while keeping the existing `fopen()` behavior on Windows where POSIX permissions don't apply in the same way. Concretely:
- Under non-Windows builds, call `open(dest_path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR)`.
- Check the returned file descriptor for errors and log/clean up as now.

## Summary

Two new tools for validating gene regulatory predictions against experimental Perturb-seq knockdown data (Replogle et al., Cell 2022):

body:
Several bugs in `code.gs` and `form.html` cause crashes, silent failures, and corrupted file uploads. This PR addresses the critical issues.

## `code.gs`

- **Null-pointer crash on regex mismatch** — `.match()` result was used without a null-check; now returns a structured error if the Drive URL doesn't contain a file ID
- **Corrupted image uploads** — `base64Decode` was called with `Charset.UTF_8`, which mangles binary data; removed the charset argument
- **No server-side validation** — required text fields and both file uploads are now validated before touching Drive/Sheets
- **Unsanitized filenames** — client-supplied filenames are now stripped of non-alphanumeric characters before being passed to Drive

```js
// Before — crashes when match() returns null
const photoMatch = photoLink.match(/\/d\/([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)/);
const photoFileId = photoMatch[1]; // 💥

// After
const photoMatch = photoLink.match(/\/d\/([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)/);
if (!photoMatch) return { status: 'error', message: 'Could not extract photo file ID from Drive URL.' };
```

## `form.html`

- **Silent server failures** — `google.script.run` now chains `.withErrorHandler()` so errors reach the user
- **Files were effectively optional** — photo and signature are now validated as required before async encoding begins
- **No file-size guard** — added a 5 MB client-side limit per file to prevent quota exhaustion
- **`console.debug` in production** — removed all debug logging from the submit flow, `resetForm`, Vanta init, and the debug-only `watchVantaCanvas` interval
